question:
A 16-year-old female presents with a sore throat and breathing difficulties. She developed cough,
congestion, runny nose, low-grade fever, and body aches two days ago. Today, her cough worsened
and began producing yellow phlegm. She reports shortness of breath, and her mother noticed a “funny
sound” with her breathing that started this afternoon. She has had reduced appetite and minimal fluid
intake. She is fully vaccinated, including for Covid-19, and SARS-CoV-2 testing is negative. On
examination, her temperature is 39.0°C, heart rate is 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 27
breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 90% on room air. She appears tired, anxious, and ill, with
increased work of breathing. Examination reveals nasal congestion but no drooling. Audible inspiratory
stridor and moderate intercostal retractions are noted, which do not improve with racemic epinephrine.
Breath sounds are present bilaterally without wheezing or rales. The remainder of the physical exam is
unremarkable. Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible for this patient’s condition?
Answer Choices: (A) Group A Streptococcus (B) Parainfluenza virus type 1 (C) Haemophilus
influenzae type b (D) Mycoplasma pneumoniae (E) Staphylococcus aureus (F) Adenovirus (G)
Influenza A virus (H) Respiratory syncytial virus (I) Epstein-Barr virus (J) Corynebacterium diphtheriae
 A. Staphylococcus aureus
B. Respiratory syncytial virus
C. Group A Streptococcus
D. Influenza A virus
E. Corynebacterium diphtheriae
F. Parainfluenza virus type 1
G. Haemophilus influenzae type b
H. Epstein-Barr virus
I. Adenovirus
J. Mycoplasma pneumoniae
